graph.title: LEGO Architecture 21033 Chicago
notes: Total piece count matches the 444-piece inventory: 189 plain nodes (b1-b189) plus 255 inside repeats (redA 28, redB 24, deck 18, wfl 45, wmid 21, wcross 25, bhouse 12, leaf 4, hbeam 16, hfac 62).

Ids b1-b189 follow build order; repeat groups slot in where the manual builds them: redA/redB/deck at steps 36-46, wfl/wmid/wcross at steps 59-73, bhouse/leaf at steps 78-79, hbeam at step 98, hfac at steps 100-110.

Most piece-to-piece attachments are read from small isometric drawings. Where the exact stud or plate is not clear, I picked the nearest plausible underlying piece and left ports null. This applies especially to the surface tiles and jumpers at steps 32-35 and the Wrigley side plates at steps 85-89.

The inventory has one colour per element id, so the colour of ambiguous grey pieces (black vs dark bluish grey vs light bluish grey) is inferred from the parts-list totals. Willis Tower 1x2, 1x1 and 1x3 plates, and the black vs dark-grey 1x1 tiles at steps 64, 72 and 74-75, were assigned so each colour total matches the inventory.
Steps 52, 57 and 30/48 (flips) have no parts and are not edges. The Willis base plate (b92) and Big Red (redA1.core on b87) are attached to the base by assumed stud contacts.

Hancock pillar stacking order (b170 up to b169) is inferred from the 6 mini-steps on pages 97-98. The two black beams (hbeam) clip onto the 18649 handle plate at the top and onto the base's dark-tan handle plates b32/b34 at the bottom. These are clip/bar joints and are revolute.
Wrigley sits on the rotating turntable top (b51), which is hinged to the turntable base b56. The two bridge leaves clip onto the two clip tiles b50/b81 and are revolute.
The manual presents parts boxes for steps 100-110 as per-assembly counts, so hfac is built twice, and for step 98 as totals across both hbeam copies; this was reconciled with the inventory totals.
